closer.name: Open
closer.note: No incumbent. Jacob Webb re-signed ($2M for 2027, $4M club option for 2028) as the cheap bridge.

depth.label: Projected 2027 starters

lineup.name: Miguel Amaya
lineup.note: Starter by default. Joey Bart, claimed Friday, is the likely partner: .214/.305/.357 and an 82 OPS+ in 2026, one arbitration year left (MLBTR projects $2.9M). Kelly is still a free agent; prospect Owen Ayers is the in-house fallback.

lineup.name: Michael Busch
lineup.note: 106 OPS+. First base was the only position where the Cubs had negative DRS.

lineup.name: Alex Bregman
lineup.note: Year 2 of 5 years, $175M. Won his second Gold Glove Sunday, the first Cubs third baseman to win since Ron Santo.

lineup.name: Open
lineup.note: Adams (MLBTR) expects Ramírez to get the first look, with Shaw a maybe. Boston tendered Duran Friday, so he's a trade-only option. Trevor Larnach was non-tendered by Minnesota and is a free agent. Kwan isn't moving before the lockout.

lineup.name: Pete Crow-Armstrong
lineup.note: 2026 NL MVP, unanimous (30 of 30 first-place votes). 6-year, $115M extension starts in 2027. Platinum Glove: +26 OAA led baseball.

lineup.name: Open
lineup.note: Suzuki rejected the $23.15M QO and is a free agent; MLBTR projects four years, $105M. Passan says the Padres met him Monday and may be the favorite. Comp pick after the fourth round if he signs elsewhere. Alcántara is out of options and gets a long look in spring.

lineup.name: Open
lineup.note: Conforto is a free agent. Adams (MLBTR) lists him and Tyrone Taylor as likely 'modest veteran' reunions if Suzuki and Happ both leave.

depth.note: As of Nov. 21. Still no starters. Tender day: claimed C Joey Bart, got RHP Braxton Roxby for cash, non-tendered Gabriel Arias and Ethan Roberts. 40-man at 37. Suzuki is a free agent; Brown (neck surgery) out until about midseason.

rotation.name: Edward Cabrera
rotation.note: Under control. 5.96 ERA in 2026. Hawkins wouldn't promise him a spot: 'Got to get some outs out of him.'

rotation.name: Justin Steele
rotation.note: Elbow. No MLB start since April 2025.

rotation.name: Open
rotation.note: All five 2026 finishers are gone and Brown is out until midseason. Still linked: King (Morosi), Peralta (Bowden: six-plus teams), Rogers (Sharma; costs two picks), Taira (Levine; Mets in too), Itoh (visited Nov. 20). Morosi expects King and Peralta to wait until Skubal signs. May, Gray and the Mariners' trade arms are gone.

rotation.name: Open
rotation.note: Brown is out until around midseason after neck surgery. Assad, Jordan Wicks and Braxton Garrett are what's left in-house. This slot has to be bought now, too.

headline: The Mets put nearly $400 million in front of Skubal, and Morosi says King and Peralta won't sign until he does. The Cubs' window is shrinking toward Dec. 1.

injuries.injury: UCL revision repair with an internal brace (April 16, 2026)
injuries.name: Cade Horton
injuries.return: Second half of 2027 at the earliest (15-16 month timeline)

injuries.injury: Left elbow surgery (April 2025); a flexor strain wiped out his 2026 return
injuries.name: Justin Steele
injuries.note: Three rehab outings at Triple-A Iowa in September: 6.35 ERA over 5 2/3 innings. 2027 is the last year of his contract.

injuries.injury: Cervical spine (neck) surgery, Nov. 9, 2026, after a stress fracture in a neck vertebra ended his season
injuries.name: Ben Brown
injuries.note: Hawkins called it 'an aggressive move' aimed at getting him a starter's workload long term. Had a growth removed from his neck in 2024. First-time arbitration eligible (Super Two), projected $1.3M.
injuries.return: Throwing early 2027; MLB return around midseason (Hawkins)

injuries.injury: UCL reconstruction with an internal brace (April 20, 2026)
injuries.name: Porter Hodge
Shelby Miller
injuries.return: 2027, final year of a two-year deal

injuries.injury: Left elbow inflammation and flexor strain
injuries.name: Riley Martin

lastSummary: The Padres finished a two-game sweep with a 4-1 win at Petco. Kevin Gausman lasted 3 1/3 innings and took the loss, and Daniel Palencia gave up the back-breaking hit to Gavin Sheets. Bregman and Crow-Armstrong went a combined 0-for-15 with eight strikeouts in the series, and the highest-scoring offense in baseball managed one run in 18 innings.
parkNote: Wrigley has played slightly pitcher-friendly overall (96 run factor, 2024-26) while boosting homers (106). The Cubs posted an .789 OPS at home and .747 on the road.
preview: Now: Skubal has a nine-year, near-$400M Mets offer (Duquette) and is expected to pick by Dec. 1. Morosi says King and Peralta sign after he does.
Now: Itoh visited Chicago Friday (Jorge Castillo, ESPN). He, Taira and Sato must sign by Dec. 1 no matter what Skubal does. That's the lane the Cubs control.
Next: Monday's market for fresh non-tenders. Ober, Larnach and Gorman are free agents.
Dec. 1: CBA expires. Every rotation slot past Cabrera, Steele and Assad still has to be bought before then.

stats.label: Starting pitchers added this offseason. Tender day brought a backup catcher and a Triple-A reliever.
The Mets' reported nine-year offer to Skubal (Duquette). Morosi says King and Peralta wait on his answer.

items.call: Petriello's read is right: over four years Suzuki is the better bet. Letting him go for a comp pick only works if the money buys arms this week.
items.detail: Passan (ESPN): San Diego met with Suzuki on Monday and may be the favorite (via MLB.com, Nov. 18). The Padres also lost seven starters and are meeting Skubal Wednesday. Nov. 21: Mike Petriello (MLB.com) finds Suzuki and Arozarena with identical four-year lines (14 fWAR, about 30% better than average) and leans Suzuki on bat speed (63rd percentile), chase (89th) and a +7 FRV year in right. Red flag: his hard-hit rate fell 10 points, a top-five drop.
items.name: Padres may be the favorite for Suzuki

items.call: Fine as the backup. Wrong if it's the Kelly replacement. Amaya plus Bart is the weakest catching pair the Cubs have run in years, and Kelly is still sitting there on a two-year deal.
items.detail: Claimed Friday (Feinsand, MLB.com) after Chicago's AL club DFA'd him Tuesday; the Cubs avoided arbitration with him, terms not disclosed (MLB.com via MLB Korea). 29, former No. 2 overall pick. .214/.305/.357, 4 HR, 82 OPS+ in 128 PA for Pittsburgh, Atlanta and the White Sox; broke his left hand Aug. 6. 120 wRC+ in 80 games for the 2024 Pirates. Last arbitration year; MLBTR had projected $2.9M.
items.name: Joey Bart (waiver claim, White Sox)

items.call: Optionable depth for Iowa. Better than another out-of-options claim. Still not pitching help.
items.detail: 27, debuted Aug. 28; 3.38 ERA over 5 1/3 MLB innings with the Giants. 3.78 ERA, 60 K, 26 BB in 64 1/3 Triple-A innings. Has minor-league options (CubsHQ). Washington had claimed him Oct. 29.
items.name: Braxton Roxby (trade, Nationals, for cash)

items.call: Right on both. The infield depth behind Swanson is now thin, so a minor-league reunion for Arias wouldn't be crazy.
items.detail: Both are free agents (MLB.com). Arias: 10 PA as a Cub after the August claim, projected $1.3M. Roberts: 4.21 ERA in 23 games in 2026, 4.70 career. Nine others tendered: Amaya, Busch, Garrett, Rolison, Steele, Assad, Brown, Cabrera, Palencia (MLB.com via MLB Korea). 40-man at 37.
items.name: Gabriel Arias, Ethan Roberts non-tendered

items.call: Sign him as the No. 5. Two years at that price is the cheapest real starter on the board, and a 5% walk rate plays. He's the floor, not the answer.
items.detail: Visited Chicago Friday, per ESPN's Jorge Castillo (via CubsHQ); both Chicago clubs need arms, and the White Sox had already been linked (Romero, Nov. 15). 29, 2025 Sawamura winner; 3.18 ERA, 159 K, 34 BB over 172 2/3 innings in 2026. MLBTR projects two years, $20M. Must sign by Dec. 1.
items.name: Hiromi Itoh (NPB, posted)

items.call: Larnach was on Adams' cheap-LF list, and now he costs nothing but money. Ober is a one-year rotation flier. Make calls Monday.
items.detail: Minnesota non-tendered Bailey Ober and Trevor Larnach, released Matt Wallner, and traded Lewis for Bobby Miller and a catching prospect (MLB.com). St. Louis cut Nolan Gorman; Boston cut Connor Wong. Duran and Burger were tendered.
items.name: Tender day: Ober, Larnach, Wallner, Gorman hit the market; Royce Lewis to the Dodgers
Oviedo to Arizona, Melton extended, Doval stays in San Francisco
items.detail: Arizona got RHP Johan Oviedo from Boston for minor-league LHP Luke Dotson and a PTBNL or cash; he missed most of 2026 with an elbow sprain (MLB.com). Detroit extended Troy Melton six years, $46.5M guaranteed, after a 2.76 ERA in 20 starts. The Giants kept Camilo Doval for one year, reportedly $6.3M, and sent Christian Koss to the Rays.
items.call: Oviedo for a Class A lefty is the kind of cheap rotation flier the Cubs should be scooping. Another one gone.
This is the internal-options pitch for the corners. It lines up with Hawkins' Nov. 13 comments. Fine for one spot. Not for two, and not if it means the Suzuki money never gets spent.
items.detail: Daily Herald (Nov. 20): Kelly said there's 'a version of [Busch] somewhere in between' his 2025 breakout and his 2026 drop, and the club is 'excited about Matt Shaw being healthy.' Happ, Suzuki, Kelly and Taylor are all free agents.
items.name: Hitting coach Dustin Kelly backs Busch and a healthy Shaw

items.call: No free lunch now. Boston will want something for him, and every Cubs trade chip should buy pitching. Pass unless the price is a fringe prospect.
items.detail: Boston tendered him Friday; he isn't on MLB.com's non-tender list, so he's trade-only now. Mooney (The Athletic, Nov. 19): the Cubs evaluated him 'as a potential change-of-scenery addition.' MLBTR projects $11.1M. 76 OPS+ and .207/.266/.361 in 2026; 10.4 fWAR across 2024-25. Fox notes Boston has asked about Suzuki to replace him.
items.name: Jarren Duran (trade, Red Sox)

items.call: Wrong call to sit out, and now it's moot: the Mets just set the price near $400M. The real cost of skipping him is the clock. Everyone else's plan waits on his decision; the Cubs' can't.
items.detail: Passan (ESPN, Nov. 19): the Mets are the favorite, partly because the Dodgers want a shorter commitment. He met the Dodgers and Blue Jays this week and has the Padres next; Passan says it will be the biggest pitcher contract ever. Sharma (The Athletic) reported the Cubs plan to sit out the bidding (Nov. 9). MLBTR projects nine years, $425M. Nov. 19: the Padres met him too, and Heyman says new ownership will back an 'ultra-aggressive' Preller, though the Mets remain the expected landing spot (via MLB.com). Nov. 20: a fifth, undisclosed team met him over Zoom (Heyman via MLB.com); he's expected to pick by Dec. 1. Nov. 20: Jim Duquette reports the Mets made a nine-year offer for almost $400 million, which would be the highest AAV ever for a free-agent starter (via MLB.com).
items.name: Tarik Skubal (free agent)

items.call: Gone, and the Cubs were never on his list. That's another sinkerballer they could have had for two years. Morejon is the last impact reliever left; get in.
items.detail: Signed Friday (Jorge Castillo, ESPN, via Fox Sports). 2.42 ERA, 1.03 WHIP, 172 ERA+ over 67 innings with Arizona in 2026. MLBTR had projected two years, $13M. The Yankees also kept Tim Hill earlier (1 yr, $2.25M).
items.name: Loaisiga back to the Yankees (2 yr, club option for 2029)

items.call: Sign him as the No. 2, not the only add. If he waits on Skubal, the Skubal losers come for him with money already budgeted. Make the offer now.
items.detail: Declined his player option. 3.21 ERA in 185 innings, but 21.0% K and 9.2% BB were career worsts (FanGraphs). Morosi (Nov. 13) called King-Cubs a 'pairing that many of us have forecasted'; on Nov. 20 he said the White Sox are in on King too (MLB.com). MLBTR projects four years, $92M. Morosi (Nov. 20) thinks King and Peralta won't sign until after Skubal decides (MLB.com).
items.name: Michael King (free agent)

items.call: This is the one to win. Don't wait for Skubal: put four years at a premium AAV in front of him with a deadline, before the Jays, Dodgers or Padres lose the Skubal race and pivot.
items.detail: Jim Bowden (Nov. 20): more than six teams are in, including the Padres, both Chicago clubs and the Rays, maybe the Braves (via SI, MLB.com). Morosi says the White Sox are on King and Peralta too. Rosenthal (Nov. 13) called him an 'obvious fit' because Counsell managed him. MLBTR projects five years, $110M; FanGraphs four years, $92M. Morosi (Nov. 20): Peralta and King likely sign after Skubal does.
items.name: Freddy Peralta (free agent)

items.call: Fine as a development plan, dangerous as a roster plan. A blister-prone 5.96 ERA is not one of the two arms they need. If the front office counts a fixed Cabrera as an addition, the winter already failed.
items.detail: MLB.com (Casey Drottar, Nov. 19): Hoyer said the club 'struggled with Edward' and has to own not getting the most out of him. Hawkins blamed blisters and said fixing his fingers is the priority; VP of pitching strategy Tyler Zombro checks in with him every morning. Cabrera gave the Cubs 80 innings of 5.96 ERA after costing the No. 1 prospect.
items.name: Hoyer, Hawkins: 'We have to get more out of' Cabrera

items.call: Two more mid-rotation trade arms off the board, and Colorado got them for a lefty and a catching prospect. That's the price range the Cubs should have been working in. The trade tier is thinning as fast as the free-agent tier.
items.detail: ESPN (Nov. 19): Colorado acquires right-handers Castillo and Martin; the White Sox get LHP Sean Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz. Also Nov. 19: the Royals and Randy Dobnak agreed to a one-year, $1.35M deal.
items.name: Rockies get Luis Castillo, Davis Martin from the White Sox

items.call: Free lottery ticket with a real strikeout rate, and it costs a roster spot they weren't using. Fine. Just don't let anyone count it as pitching help. Expect him back on waivers before spring.
items.detail: Claimed Thursday; Heyman had it first (MLBTR). 28, out of options, 10.18 career ERA over 20 1/3 MLB innings with Baltimore, the Dodgers and the Mets. Since 2023 in the minors: 3.99 ERA, 30.5% K, 14.6% BB over 320 innings. The Mets had signed him for 2027 and tried to slip him through waivers. No corresponding move; the 40-man is at 37.
items.name: Chayce McDermott (waiver claim, Mets)

items.call: Another bidder on the exact one-year bounce-back tier the Cubs would use to fill SP5. Bubic is the best of those bets. Make the offer before Baltimore or Washington does.
items.detail: Spencer Nusbaum (The Athletic, via MLBTR, Nov. 19): Washington prefers short free-agent deals and has asked about Kris Bubic, Brady Singer and Kona Takahashi. Bubic: 2.98 ERA and 25.5% K over 217 1/3 innings since 2023, but only 55 innings in 2026 around elbow trouble.
items.name: Nationals want short-term starters: Bubic, Singer, Takahashi

items.call: Sign him, and outbid San Diego, the Mets and the White Sox by a year if that's what it takes. Nine suitors means 'interest' is worth nothing. But 146 innings is his career high, so he's a No. 3 or 4, not the fix. If he's the only arm by Dec. 1, the winter failed.
items.detail: Bruce Levine (670 The Score) now counts nine teams in, the Cubs among them (via Bleacher Nation, Nov. 19); earlier he said both Chicago clubs had 'strong' interest. The Mets set a Zoom (Heyman); the Padres, Blue Jays and Giants are in too. 27, 5'8", 1.36 ERA, 141 K in 146 innings in 2026; mostly a reliever until this year. McDaniel (ESPN) floated five years, $72.5M plus a $12M+ posting fee; Bowden had three years, $30M. He must sign before the lockout.
items.name: Kaima Taira (NPB, posted)

items.call: Scouting him is fine. Paying for him before two starters land is not. A 66% contact bat is a DH bet, and Bregman owns third. If the arms get done first, he's a smarter corner gamble than an $11M Duran.
items.detail: Patrick Mooney (The Athletic, Nov. 19) says the Cubs have 'extensively scouted' him (via MLB.com, CBS). Central League Triple Crown: .306/.383/.609, 39 HR, 106 RBI in 143 games. 66% contact rate vs. a 77% MLB average (CBS). Mostly a third baseman, with outfield time; most clubs see first base, a corner or DH long term. Also linked to the Mets, Yankees, Dodgers and Phillies.
items.name: Teruaki Sato (NPB, posted)

items.call: Fine to lose the player at that price for a 37-year-old with a fading fastball. Not fine that he was one of the Cubs' own linked names and nobody even reported a Cubs offer. That's three linked arms gone this week: May, Gray, and the Mariners' trade door.
items.detail: Announced Wednesday (MLBTR, Nov. 18; Heyman first had the $55M). $20M in 2027, then a $30M player option for 2028 with a $5M buyout, so it works like an opt-out after one year. 2.72 ERA over 169 innings and fifth in AL Cy Young voting, but the four-seamer fell to a career-low 91.5 mph and he allowed in-zone contact at a career-high 92.1%.
items.name: Sonny Gray to the Twins (2 yr, $55M)

items.call: That kills the Kirby-Hancock idea. Seattle wanted a third baseman and got one from Kansas City, not from the Cubs' spare young bats. The Cubs had the pieces and the need, and the Royals made the deal.
items.detail: Six players: Seattle gets 3B Maikel Garcia (five years, $57.5M, through 2030), RP James McArthur and LHP prospect L.P. Langevin; Kansas City gets Miller, Evans and LHP Jose A. Ferrer (Passan, Divish, Rosenthal via MLBTR). Dipoto told the Seattle Times there is 'zero' chance of trading another starter. Seattle's 2027 rotation: Gilbert, Woo, Kirby, Hancock and Anderson.
items.name: Mariners trade Bryce Miller, Logan Evans to the Royals; Dipoto: 'zero' chance of another starter deal

items.call: The market for the Cubs' top target just added the Mets. Rymer (Bleacher Report) already predicts Taira to the White Sox at four years, $68M. If the Cubs want him, they have to bid like it this week, not 'show interest.'
items.detail: Heyman (NY Post): the Mets set a Zoom meeting with Taira. MLBTR lists the Padres, Blue Jays and 'both Chicago clubs' as interested and says he 'will almost certainly sign in the next two weeks' (Franco, Nov. 18). Separately, Franco reports the White Sox are after another notable starter after May, naming Taira and Rogers among the options.
items.name: Mets schedule Taira; White Sox want another starter

items.call: Treat Dec. 1 as a hard wall. Anything the Cubs don't buy in the next 12 days is likely off the table until spring, and the players who sign in that window are the ones with deadlines: Taira and the QO guys.
items.detail: At the owners' meetings Wednesday: 'They want salary cap and floor, and on that, we will not compromise.' MLBPA chief Bruce Meyer called it 'a radical change to the system.' A Dec. 2 lockout is 'all but officially guaranteed' (MLBTR, Nov. 18). The last one ran 99 days.
items.name: Manfred: MLB 'will not compromise' on cap and floor

items.call: Now he's a real option, and he's the 'impact arm' Hoyer keeps promising. Five years for a reliever is too long. Three years at a higher AAV, picks and all, is worth it for a pen that blew 28 saves.
items.detail: Turned down the $23.15M offer Tuesday and wants to stay a reliever; MLB.com lists the Mets, Cubs and Giants as fits (via MLB Data Warehouse, Nov. 18). MLBTR projects five years, $80M. 99.1 mph, 30.4% K, 2.83 ERA over 86 innings. Signing him costs the Cubs two picks and $1M in pool money.
items.name: Adrian Morejon rejects the Padres' QO

items.call: Done deal, and the 'interest' line is politeness. Take the pick and don't chase him past three years. The money goes to an arm.
items.detail: Rejected the $23.15M QO Tuesday (Alden González, ESPN). .270, 26 HR, 86 RBI, .841 OPS, career-high 81 walks, +7 fielding run value in 2026 (MLB.com). MLBTR projects four years, $105M. Hawkins: 'We would be silly not to have interest in reuniting with him.' Linked to the Phillies, Blue Jays and Royals (USA Today). Comp pick lands after the fourth round. Passan: the Padres met him Monday and may be the favorite.
items.name: Seiya Suzuki

items.call: Off the board. The Cubs had the young bats Seattle wanted and let the Royals beat them to it.
items.detail: Dead. Dipoto told the Seattle Times there is 'zero' chance of trading another starter after Miller and Evans went to Kansas City for Maikel Garcia (MLBTR, Nov. 18). Kirby and Hancock are in Seattle's 2027 rotation.
items.name: George Kirby, Emerson Hancock (trade, Mariners)

items.call: Gone. Scratch him from the list.
items.detail: Signed with Minnesota Nov. 18: two years, $55M, with an effective opt-out after 2027 (MLBTR).
items.name: Sonny Gray (signed, Twins)

items.call: Triple-A depth. A 5.9 BB/9 career walk rate is not the 'impact arm' Hoyer promised.
items.detail: Announced by his agency Nov. 17; terms unknown, likely not a guaranteed deal (Cubs Insider). Career 5.34 ERA, 254 K and 146 BB in 246 innings with the Rockies, Pirates, Twins and Nationals.
items.name: Justin Lawrence (likely minor-league deal)

items.call: Deserved. It also tells you where the 2027 problem isn't. The best lineup and best defense in the NL lost a Wild Card sweep because the pitching was thin. Fix the staff.
items.detail: PCA's first, Bregman's second, and the franchise's first team Silver Slugger. Cubs Insider says they're the first team to win the team Silver Slugger and team Gold Glove in the same season.
items.name: PCA, Bregman and the team win Silver Sluggers

items.call: Fair price, and the Cubs shouldn't mourn the player. They should mourn the pace. The crosstown team is now one arm up, and $17.5M a year for a 4.70 ERA just set the floor for the Holmes-Peterson tier.
items.detail: Agreed Tuesday; agent Craig Rose confirmed $52.5M to Jon Heyman after Robert Murray's first report (MLBTR, Nov. 17). 4.70 ERA, 3.63 FIP and 3.99 SIERA over a career-high 145 2/3 innings in 2026, 96.9 mph four-seamer. Strikeout rate has sat around 21-22% since 2023.
items.name: Dustin May to the White Sox (3 yr, $52.5M)

items.call: Jeffers staying in Minnesota takes the top catcher off the board. That makes Carson Kelly the best realistic catcher add. Sign him on two years before someone else does.
items.detail: Bednar took $23.15M from the Yankees, the biggest one-year salary ever for a reliever (Hoch, MLB.com). Jeffers took the Twins' QO, reversing reports he'd decline (Gleeman). Five others rejected: Suzuki, Arozarena, Rogers, Brandon Lowe, Morejon (Alden González, ESPN, via MLBTR).
items.name: Bednar and Jeffers accept QOs

items.call: Right calls, both. Neither is a 2027 rotation answer. Wiggins was the Detmers trade chip at the deadline, so protecting him keeps that deal alive.
items.detail: Protected from the Rule 5 draft Tuesday; the 40-man is at 36 (MLBTR). Wiggins, Baseball America's No. 4 Cubs prospect: upper-90s heat, 2.19 ERA and 31% K in 2025, then a 6.75 ERA and 17.3% walk rate in 42 2/3 innings around elbow trouble in 2026. McCullough: 3.27 ERA, 27.7% K over 55 innings, mostly Double-A. Starter or reliever for Wiggins gets decided in spring.
items.name: Jaxon Wiggins, Brody McCullough added to the 40-man

items.call: Pay it, picks included. He's the best realistic No. 2 left, and May's $17.5M AAV just showed what the tier below him costs. Five years is the line; don't go to six.
items.detail: Formally rejected the Orioles' QO Tuesday (MLBTR, Baltimore Banner). Sharma (The Athletic) says the Cubs are interested and are contacting almost every starter. 3.16 ERA, 23.2% K and 6.1% BB over 48 starts since 2025; 7.3 fWAR. As a 2026 tax payor, the Cubs would lose their second- and fifth-highest 2027 picks plus $1M in international pool money. MLBTR predicts five years, $115M. Baltimore still prefers him among its lefty targets (Kostka).
items.name: Trevor Rogers (free agent)

items.call: Baltimore is a direct rival for Rogers and the Peterson fallback. That's two more bidders on the exact arms the Cubs are 'contacting.' Pick one and move.
items.detail: Kostka (Baltimore Banner) says Baltimore is leaning left-handed: Rogers first, then Kris Bubic and Matthew Boyd; he names Peterson as a possible fit. Robert Murray (FanSided) reports several teams are interested in Peterson (MLBTR, Nov. 16). Baltimore has $40M+ of room.
items.name: Orioles chase lefties: Rogers, Bubic, Boyd

items.call: Correct. One year as the No. 5 at most, and only after two real starters are signed.
items.detail: No QO. Declined his side of the $15M mutual option ($2M buyout). 3.91 ERA, 18.5% K rate. Turns 36 in February. The Orioles are interested (Kostka) and he's been tied to the Padres. MLBTR projects one year, $13M.
items.name: Matthew Boyd

items.call: Re-sign him, two years, as the No. 4. If he's the headline of the winter, the winter failed.
items.detail: 114 ERA+ in 15 starts after the June trade, 4.06 FIP, 10.2% walk rate. Sharma reports the Cubs are working to bring him back. Robert Murray (FanSided) says several teams are interested, and the Banner's Kostka names him as a fit for lefty-hungry Baltimore (MLBTR, Nov. 16). MLBTR projects two years, $24M.
items.name: David Peterson

items.call: The crosstown team just made Taira a real bidding war. Overpay by a year or a few million now. A Boras client with a hard deadline is the one time waiting costs you the player, not just the price.
items.detail: Francys Romero (BeisbolFR) says the Sox sent scouts to watch both in August and September. Itoh, the 2025 Sawamura winner, projects at two years, $20M (MLBTR, Nov. 15). All three NPB posts went up Nov. 1, so roughly two weeks remain.
items.name: White Sox scouted Taira and Itoh

items.call: Only if the cost is a bat, not an arm. A former No. 2 pick who hasn't hit is the same bet as Ramírez or Shaw in a corner. The Cubs already have three of those.
items.detail: North Side Baseball's Randy Holt calls Crews an upside gamble worth taking. He's reportedly available as a change-of-scenery candidate, and the Cubs need a corner outfielder (via Bleed Cubbie Blue, Nov. 15). Opinion piece, no reported talks.
items.name: Dylan Crews (trade, Nationals)

items.call: This is the real threat. The Padres are chasing the same middle tier the Cubs are, and they're moving faster. Every day the Cubs wait, the Imanaga-Peterson-King price goes up and the list gets shorter.
items.detail: San Diego is losing seven starters and needs four or five rotation arms. Acee (Union-Tribune) says they've checked on nearly every free-agent starter, including Boyd, Imanaga and May; Gonzalez (ESPN) adds Peralta and Nick Martinez. Morosi has them meeting Skubal and eyeing King and Pivetta reunions (MLB.com, Nov. 14).
items.name: Padres in on Imanaga, Boyd, Peralta, Martinez

items.call: Bring him back on two years. At those prices he's the most reliable starter available to them.
items.detail: 112 ERA+ in 32 starts, 35 homers allowed. Not QO-eligible. Barely linked anywhere so far; Morosi named the Tigers as a possible suitor Friday (Bleacher Nation). MLBTR projects two years, $40M; FanGraphs two years, $28M.
items.name: Shota Imanaga

items.call: Job security is not the problem. Urgency is. A president signed through 2030 can afford to sit out Skubal; a team with zero starters can't. Domingues is the right kind of hire for the right department.
items.detail: The Athletic's Mooney and Sharma report the extension Hoyer signed in mid-2025 runs five years, which puts him under contract through 2030 (via MLBTR, Nov. 13). The Cubs also hired Rylan Domingues, a Phillies pitching development analyst for three years, as pitching analytics coordinator.
items.name: Hoyer's extension: five years, through 2030

items.call: Two things for the Cubs: a one-year breakout bat just got four years, so Suzuki's price only goes up, and Boston now has to move an outfielder. Good for the Duran talks.
items.detail: The first big deal of the winter, per Passan (ESPN). Turned down Milwaukee's $23.15M QO; Boston gives up its second- and fifth-highest picks and the Brewers get a pick at the end of the first round (MLBTR). 143 wRC+, 3.6 fWAR and NLCS MVP in 2026; he's 31 (Bleacher Nation).
items.name: Jake Bauers to the Red Sox (4 yr, $58M)

items.call: That's the plan in plain words: go cheap at three spots to pay for pitching. Fine, if the pitching actually arrives. Ramírez's .315 wOBA sat on a .283 xwOBA and he's barely played the outfield. Bring Kelly back on two years and sign one real corner bat.
items.detail: 'There's a risk to going with some unproven guys, but that allows you maybe to get some more proven guys in other spots.' And: 'I don't think there's one path that we necessarily would cross out.' Ramírez, Shaw and Alcántara are the in-house corner options; the catcher fallback is Amaya plus Owen Ayers (Montemurro, Tribune, via MLBTR, Nov. 13). Hoyer: 'We're not going to be able to bring back all of them.'
items.name: Hawkins: corners and catcher may be filled internally

items.call: Not a Cubs fit. Hoerner's extension starts in 2027 and the money is for arms. Watch it only as a sign of how fast front offices are moving before the lockout.
items.detail: Piecoro (Arizona Republic): Arizona met Marte's agent at the GM Meetings without learning which teams he'd accept. Full 10-and-5 rights, about $91.75M owed, and any deal must close by Dec. 1 (MLBTR).
items.name: Ketel Marte talks stuck on his no-trade list

items.call: Fermin is the cheap version of the Kelly plan. Glove first, three years of control, and it costs a mid-tier prospect, not $10M a year. If Kelly wants two guaranteed years, take Fermin and pair him with Amaya.
items.detail: San Diego is likely to move one of them with Ethan Salas taking over (Acee, via MLBTR, Nov. 12). The Cubs are listed among a dozen teams in the backup-catcher market. Fermin: .203/.274/.315, elite blocking and framing, about $2.6M projected, three years of control, two options. Campusano: .265/.363/.433 in 248 PA, poor framer, out of options.
items.name: Freddy Fermin, Luis Campusano (trade, Padres)

items.call: One fewer high-leverage arm on the board, and it sets the price: about $11-12M a year for a good reliever. The Cubs can pay that. They need to.
items.detail: $11M in 2027 and 2028, $13M in 2029. 3.46 ERA, 33 K in 26 innings after Tommy John; 96.8 mph and a sweeper hitters went 2-for-34 against (MLB.com).
items.name: Evan Phillips to the Braves (3 yr, $35M)

items.call: Deserved, and it wasn't close. Now the real point: the best player in the league costs $19M a year through 2032. That surplus has a use, and it's pitching. Waste it on a hope-based rotation and the MVP is a footnote.
items.detail: All 30 first-place votes, 420 points; Ohtani second (264), Turang third. First unanimous MVP in Cubs history, first Cubs MVP since Bryant in 2016. .280/.372/.570, 45 HR, 41 SB, 119 runs, 357 total bases, 9.8+ bWAR. Also the Hank Aaron Award, All-MLB First Team and the Platinum Glove (BBWAA, Bleed Cubbie Blue).
items.name: PCA wins NL MVP, unanimously

items.call: Good for the Cubs' comp pick. A weak bat market with two similar corner outfielders means Suzuki gets paid elsewhere. Don't match it.
items.detail: Boras wants six years, $150M+; MLBTR predicts four years, $100M. Phillies are the only team linked. Boston may move Jarren Duran, which could open a run at Suzuki or Arozarena (MLBTR, Nov. 11).
items.name: Arozarena's market sets Suzuki's

payroll.label: Room under the tax threshold (Cubbies Crib)
CBA expires (lockout all but certain Dec. 2)

stove.summary: Still no starters with 10 days left. The Mets reportedly offered Skubal nine years and almost $400 million, and Morosi says King and Peralta will wait until Skubal picks, which crams the Cubs' two biggest targets into the last days before the lockout. Itoh visited Friday; the NPB arms are the only lane not tied to Skubal's clock.
